title: Inversion of control

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Spring knowledge and questions
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Inversion of control means the framework creates and wires objects, instead of your code creating its own dependencies. A class declares what it needs, usually through a constructor, and the container supplies it. Dependency injection is the most common way to do IoC in Spring. The container also manages object lifetimes and scopes. The result is looser coupling and classes that are easy to test with fakes.

points.title: Who creates objects
points.why: The container creates and connects dependencies, so classes don't call new on their collaborators.

points.title: Testability
points.why: Injected dependencies can be replaced by test doubles.
